title: Correct recurrent time-limit bootstrapping
body:
With `time_limit_bootstrap=True`, the recurrent A2C/PPO/RPO/TRPO agents still add the current value at a truncation, then propagate GAE through the reset into the next episode. The recurrent state is reset at that boundary, so a later episode's rewards can incorrectly change the preceding episode's value target.

Estimate the next-state value with the critic's continuation hidden state before resetting it. For shared models, use the policy's final hidden state for that step. Discard the extra look-ahead state so it cannot advance the actual rollout twice. Pass truncation signals and the configured bootstrap mode into GAE, matching the boundary handling added to the feed-forward agents in #438.

The regressions use real `nn.RNN` models and Gymnasium `TimeLimit`, including separate/shared models and asymmetric critics. They verify stored rewards/values, continuing and reset hidden states, unchanged normalizer statistics, shared-cache consumption, and actual agent updates. In the PPO_RNN example, changing the next episode's reward from 100 to 1000 changes the old preceding return from 50.45 to 455.45; the corrected return remains 3.

[CPU validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/skrl/actions/runs/43672116748):

- Unchanged source: 33 regression assertion failures and 14 passing controls.
- Corrected regressions: 47 pass.
- Complete Torch agent/multi-agent suites: 114 pass; 67 CUDA-parameterized cases deselected.
- Repository pre-commit hooks pass, including Black, isort, and Pyright.

Tested with Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.6.0+cpu, NumPy 1.26.4, and Gymnasium 1.1.1. Disabled time-limit bootstrapping retains its existing behavior.

impact.bug: Recurrent agents with time_limit_bootstrap=True use current-state values and propagate GAE across truncation/reset boundaries
impact.fix: Compute the next-state critic value with the continuation recurrent state before reset; discard the look-ahead state; stop GAE at truncation when bootstrapping is enabled

dedup.distinction: Merged PR 438 fixes feed-forward agents but does not change any of the four recurrent files. This contribution supplies the recurrent continuation state and GAE truncation handling absent from that PR and all 21 prior forks.
dedup.excluded_duplicate_candidate: Discrete.start is already covered by open upstream PR 486.

independent_patch_integration.other_contribution: Exclude terminal states from truncation bootstrap
independent_patch_integration.note: The two source branches remain independently based on upstream. Their four overlapping reward lines must combine next-state values with the termination mask when rebasing after either merges; the exact composed source and both regression suites are verified in the combined commit.

limits: CPU float32 validation; no CUDA execution is claimed.
Complete Torch agent and multi-agent test directories were run, not all simulator/environment tests.
The change is scoped to enabled time-limit bootstrapping. Disabled mode retains the existing behavior established by the feed-forward implementation in PR 438.
Shared-model tests cover A2C_RNN, PPO_RNN and RPO_RNN; TRPO_RNN tests use separate policy and value models.
No upstream PR was created because the integration returned 403; no new merge is claimed.
